messages:
alex: Heads up — hit a surprising bug in the console bulk grant flow. If you select multiple roles and one role has an empty scope set, the inline editor shows a blank chip and when you hit Save it overwrites scopes for all roles with empty. Repro:
1) Select 3 roles
2) Click "Manage scopes" -> inline editor
3) Remove the only scope from role B (now empty)
4) Save -> role A/C scopes become empty too

maria: oh no. can you repro in prod? or just locally? :facepalm:

alex: repros in prod on the canary org I used. Happened twice. Looks like the frontend is sending a bulk PATCH with a normalized body that treats missing/empty as explicit empty list.

jen: are we doing PATCH /permissions/bulk-edit or PUT per-role under the hood ATM?

alex: current impl uses POST /permissions/bulk-edit which internally maps to a single RPC that applies the payload to each role id in the list. payload is {roles: [...], scopes: <maybe empty array | omitted>} — frontend always includes scopes field.

ravi: so bug is frontend semantics -> API applies literally. We should either (a) change frontend to omit scopes when user didn't touch that role, or (b) API should interpret empty-array as "no-op unless explicitly cleared" but that would be backwards incompatible.

sam: +1 on not breaking API contract silently. We should prefer frontend fix for now and add an explicit "Clear scopes for selected roles" checkbox to make user intent clear.

maria: UX idea: show a tri-state indicator per-scope: checked / unchecked / mixed. When editing multiple roles, default to mixed and only apply changes to roles the user touched. Provide a preview of "effective change count" before Save.

jen: makes sense. Also need telemetry: track "bulk_edit_preview_shown", "bulk_edit_role_touched" per role id (hashed) and "bulk_edit_conflict_occurred". That will help us detect regression if someone accidentally clears scopes across many tenants.

ravi: API note — we could add a query flag ?intent=explicit|intent=preserve to bulk-edit endpoint so backend can differentiate. That gives us a migration path if partners call API directly.

alex: timeline proposal: 1) quick frontend patch to omit scopes unless touched (hotfix canary today) 2) add preview + tri-state UX (next sprint) 3) instrument telemetry + analytic rule to alert if >10 roles cleared in one edit (SLO guard)

maria: what about rollback if someone already pushed bad bulk edit? Is there an audit/undo path?

sam: audit logs exist but no automated rollback. We can add a temporary compensating job that re-applies previous scope snapshots for that org if we detect mass clears (manual run for now). Longer term: enable per-bulk-edit snapshot + undo button.

jen: also check quota/rate-limit side-effects — bulk edits currently fan out into N writes in the store; doing mass undos could spike write quotas. Coordinate with eng-infra before running cleanup.

ops-bot: deploy started for canary frontend/patch at 1753216805 — watch perms.bulk_edit.* telemetry.

alex: thanks. I'll open PR for frontend omit-only-touched-scopes and attach screenshots of the tri-state mock. Will add telemetry event names to the PR description.

maria: thanks alex — please add a tiny microcopy line in preview: "Only changes you made will be applied" so admins understand the difference.

ravi: I'll follow up on the API flag proposal and sling a short design doc for review.

sam: I'll prepare an incident-runbook snippet: what to do if >50 roles cleared in <5m (pager threshold).

alex: linking PR in a sec -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7489 (WIP)

jen: nice. also add e2e for multi-select editing and a test for the empty-scope edge-case.

alex: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
